interpretation: Treat this as one activation-focused onboarding email for an existing customer account: help a new administrator connect the first drive and set the correct expectation that search becomes available when the first folder finishes indexing, not as a sales or replacement pitch.
reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): A new account administrator who has signed up but has not connected a drive..
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
reader_segment: A new account administrator who has signed up but has not connected a drive.
reader_profile_override: A new account administrator who has signed up but has not connected a drive.
promise: Connect the first drive to begin background indexing; search becomes available as soon as the first folder finishes indexing.
orientation: Portway is a searchable workspace for files in a shared drive.
arc: One self-contained activation step: orient the administrator, ask them to connect a drive, then explain exactly what happens next and when they can begin searching.
sequence_rationale: A single onboarding email should remove uncertainty around the requested first action and its immediate payoff. The documented mechanism answers the relevant timing question without inventing setup effort, total indexing duration, compatibility, security, or customer results. No separate objection or later follow-up is needed because the requested count is exactly one.

emails.selection_reason: This is the account administrator's required first activation step, and the available evidence directly explains both what connecting starts and when search becomes usable.
emails.job: Get the new account administrator to connect the first drive and understand when search becomes available.
emails.single_idea: Connect the first drive now; Portway will index it in the background, and search will work once the first folder finishes indexing.
emails.mechanism: After the administrator connects a drive, Portway indexes it in the background. The reader does not need to wait for the entire drive to finish indexing before trying search: search works as soon as the first folder finishes.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the reader does not know what happens after connecting a drive or how long they must wait to search. After: they understand that connecting starts background indexing and that search becomes available after the first folder finishes indexing.
must_not_say: Do not claim how long connecting or indexing takes.
Do not claim that setup is easy, instant, automatic beyond background indexing, or requires a specific number of steps.
Do not claim support for any particular drive provider, file type, folder structure, or technical environment.
Do not make security, privacy, compliance, pricing, support, migration, or integration claims.
Do not imply that the entire drive must finish indexing before search works.
Do not promise search quality, completeness, accuracy, time savings, adoption, or customer outcomes.
Do not introduce a sales, replacement, competitive, or urgency narrative.
emails.objection: Do I have to wait for the entire drive to finish indexing before I can search? No: search works as soon as the first folder finishes indexing.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Portway's first available search is ready to use after the first folder has finished indexing.
emails.next_step_value: Connecting the drive starts background indexing and lets the administrator verify search once the first folder finishes indexing.
emails.next_step_limit: This step does not establish total indexing time, provider compatibility, search quality, or when every file in the drive will be searchable.
emails.subject_strategy: Signal the single unfinished setup step and its near-term payoff plainly; avoid hype, urgency, or an unsupported time estimate.

voice_notes: Use the default plain, direct voice: “Hi there,” short paragraphs, first person singular where needed, and sign off “- the team.” Keep the email focused on one action and the indexing expectation.
